parsed.attack: Logging is post-hoc bookkeeping about a call you have already made: the labour falls on the caller and the benefit accrues to the sibling who wants to know it is not their turn, so the incentive is backwards for the person tapping. Within about three weeks the predictable pattern emerges - the sibling who calls most keeps logging because the ledger flatters them, the ones who call least stop logging because an entry is a confession - and the shared line reads 'Sarah rang last' three weeks running, which is not coordination, it is an accusation sitting on two people's lock screens. The moment it dies is when the least reliable sibling goes quiet: with one of three missing, 'who is up next' is simply wrong, and the other two stop trusting a line they now know is incomplete.
parsed.strongest_defence: Unlike the single-player trackers that went stale, the upkeep here has a witness who notices when it stops, and the remotely-updated Live Activity means two of the three never have to open anything to get the value - the cost of participation is one tap after a call you were making anyway. The obligation is permanent and rising, because a parent's decline increases call frequency rather than decreasing it, and invite_for_function means the group that survives week one has already done the hard part.
parsed.verdict_reason: The social witness is a real retention mechanism, but the ledger doubles as a scoreboard of who is failing, and one of three siblings going quiet in week three makes the only shared line untrustworthy.
